thread:
maya: 03:47 UTC p95 up ~4x on pv-prod-7 for /generate. stack traces show token stalls at kvcache miss + massive TCP retransmits.
liam: I'm on it. any deploys in the window?
maya: None. infra bot flagged SNAT pool at 98% for that AZ :warning:
zara: If SNAT is exhausted we'd see tail spikes due to new connections failing over to retries.
dan: conntrack: nf_conntrack_count ~260k / nf_conntrack_max 262144 — looks like we hit the ceiling. lots of TIME_WAIT.
liam: NIC counters show sudden fragmentation on eth0; MTU flipped to 1400 on some ASG nodes — config drift?
zara: Fragmentation forces kernel reassembly paths. our kernel selector chooses slower generic code on frags, which kills our optimized token loop.
maya: Also runtime kvcache eviction rate jumped; cache misses made batching windows grow while requests waited -> feedback loop.
ops-bot: deploy-check: no rolling upgrades logged. netpolicy-bot: firewall rule change at 02:59 UTC added iptables LOG and conntrack helper toggles.
liam: That LOG rule would add syscall overhead per packet and extra conntrack lookups. explains CPU + table pressure.
dan: pcap shows many small frags + SYNs; backends returning RSTs. SYNs being retried because conntrack couldn't track ephemeral ports.
zara: Root causes (prelim): 1) MTU drift -> fragmentation -> kernel fallback; 2) firewall logging toggled conntrack path; 3) SNAT port exhaustion due to conntrack/TIME_WAIT; 4) runtime batching reacted poorly to rising tail latency.
maya: Immediate mitigations applied: rolled back iptables LOG (04:10), rotated/expanded NAT IPs and increased SNAT pool (04:15), pinned ASG MTU to 1500 + restarted netagent (04:22).
liam: Also trialed a kernel-selector canary forcing user-space reassembly-avoid path on 5% traffic — p95 dropped ~30% on canary.
dan: Tuned conntrack: nf_conntrack_max -> 524288, lowered tcp TIME_WAIT pruning time, adjusted CLOSE_WAIT timeout. no host reboots.
zara: Post-mitigation: conntrack down ~80k, SNAT usage ~40%, p95 back near baseline for most routes. batching growth no longer runaway.
maya: Postmortem notes: tiny MTU drift exposed frag path; the LOG rule amplified conntrack pressure; SNAT starvation + runtime batching feedback loop created the incident.
liam: Action items:
- infra: audit MTU across private clusters + automated MTU alert
- infra: avoid enabling iptables LOG on high-throughput SNAT hosts; add gating for conntrack-heavy rules
- runtime: add guard to cap batch growth when SNAT/conntrack metrics degrade, and prefer low-latency paths
zara: I'll file infra tickets and a dashboard for fragmentation ratio. maya please draft the full postmortem with timeline + canary data.
maya: Will file the postmortem and link perf graphs. thanks all :pray:
